texts.preamble: The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Jitendra on 12 April, 2024 Author: Prem Narayan Singh Bench: Prem Narayan Singh 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Indore Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Prem Narayan Singh On The 12 th Of April, 2024 Misc. Criminal Case No. 16935 of 2018 Between:- The State Of Madhya Pradesh Food Inspector Dhar (Madhya Pradesh) (Shri Sachin Jaiswal Pl Appearing On Behalf Of Advocate General. And 1. Jitendra S/O Heeralal Ji Patidar, Aged About 52 Years, Occupation: School Sanchalak, Director Firm Patidar Bevrages Pvt. Ltd. Extension Rau, Distt. Indore Plot No. 17-18, Industrial Area Extension, Rau, Distt. Indore / R/O- 102 Prakash Nagar, Indore (Madhya Pradesh) 2. Jaymala W/O Jitendra Patidar, Aged About 50 Years, Occupation: House Work , Director Firm Patidar Bevjes Pvt. Ltd. Extation Rau, Indore, Add. Plot No.17-18, Industrial Areea Extation Rau, Indore, R/O 102, Prakash Nagar, (Madhya Pradesh) . (Shri Himanshu Joshi, Learned Counsel For The Respondent [R-1].
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant/state has submitted that the trial Court has wrongly appreciated the evidence and acquitted the respondents. It is further contended that the seized packed water will came under definition of "food" as per the Gazette notification of Govt. of India dated 21.03.2001, but the learned trial Court has acquitted the respondents without considering the same. Hence, the order of learned trial Court is not sustainable in the eyes of law. 3. On the other hand, counsel for the respondents opposed the prayer by submitting that the the pouch of water itself contains the date of expiry as one month i.e. on 20.06.2011, but the same were investigated in the laboratory on 21.07.2011 after the expiry of one month and one day. Hence, the learned trial Court has rightly acquitted the respondents. 4. That apart, it is also submitted that as per the mandatory provisions of the Act, the company has not made party in the present case. Hence, the prays for dismissal of the petition.
